description: Renovate configuration for the whole monorepo. It takes the organization defaults (7-day release age, security updates) and keeps the scope, grouping, and limits this repository chose.
The commit prefix `chore: deps:` stays (release decision R4): the release tooling gives such a commit a patch bump for its module at the next release.

packageRules.description: Keep image and action references as they are written: the organization defaults would pin every one of them to a digest.
Update only actions and reusable workflows in GitHub Actions files, not runner labels, service images, or tool versions passed to setup actions.
One pull request for all actions.
One pull request per dependency for all projects, so a version never differs between two projects of one lockfile. Clearing the group turns off the monorepo groups of the organization defaults.
Update only declared dependencies: the package manager, the engines, the peer ranges, and the overrides change by hand.
Node stays on the 24 LTS line, as in setup-workspace and the build-task-consumer image.
TypeScript 7.0 is intentionally deferred; resume updates with 7.1 and later.
One pull request per dependency for all Go modules. Each go.mod is tidied here; renovate-go-work-sync.yml brings the other modules in line with go.work on the `renovate/gomod-` branches.

backend/.go-version is the one Go version of the workspace, and tools/ci/go-version-check.sh fails on any drift, so the go and toolchain directives change by hand. A replace directive points at a local module.
A new major of a Go module at v1 or later has a new module path and needs its imports rewritten, which is a manual migration.
One pull request for the Maven reactor of the Java task consumer.
One pull request for the base images of every Dockerfile.
One pull request for the images of the Docker Compose stacks for users.
The golang builder images follow backend/.go-version in one change with the go.mod files and go.work.
Node stays on the 24 LTS line, as in setup-workspace.
Keep the plain X.Y.Z tags of qubership-core-base: the organization defaults would move them to alpine-X.Y.Z.
Keycloak tags end in a rebuild number, X.Y.Z-N, which Docker versioning reads as an incompatible suffix.
